```{r setup}
library(mysteryroster)
```

This vignette runs one synthetic registry-validity study end to end:
cross-link registries, draw a stratified sample, turn a telephone call
log into exhaustive listing statuses, and produce design-weighted
estimates, sensitivity bounds, a survey-weighted model, and study-flow
counts that are guaranteed to reconcile with each other. See
`vignette("registry-overlap")` for a deeper look at the cross-linking
step itself; this vignette starts from its output and goes the rest of
the way to an estimate.

## Building the sampling frame

Thirty NPIs, three registries. `board` and `society` are only partial
subsets of `nppes`, the frame registry everything is sampled from:

```{r frame}
ids <- sprintf("10000000%02d", 1:30)
ov <- registry_overlap(list(
  nppes   = ids,
  board   = ids[1:18],
  society = ids[10:30]
))
overlap_zone_counts(ov)

frame <- frame_strata(ov, frame = "nppes")
table(frame$stratum)
```

Three strata, not seven -- every id is in `nppes` by construction, so
the `nppes`-only zone is empty and never appears.

## Drawing a stratified sample

`stratified_listing_sample()` draws without replacement inside each
stratum and writes four design columns (`pop_N`, `n_sampled`,
`samp_frac`, `weight`) that `listing_validity_design()` needs later.
The allocation is checked against the frame before anything is drawn --
asking for more than a stratum's population stops the call rather than
drawing a smaller sample silently:

```{r sample}
sampled <- stratified_listing_sample(
  frame,
  allocation = c("nppes+board" = 5, "nppes+board+society" = 5, "nppes+society" = 6),
  seed = 20261104
)
sampled[, c("id", "stratum", "pop_N", "n_sampled", "weight")]
```

(If this sample had instead arrived as an already-completed call log
with a `stratum` column but no design columns, [listing_weights()]
attaches the same four columns from a population table directly,
without drawing anything.)

## From a call log to four exhaustive statuses

A telephone audit does not report "valid" or "invalid" -- it reports a
disposition string, which `classify_listing_status()` turns into
`physician_at_location`/`physician_active`/`invalid_reason` and one of
four exhaustive, mutually exclusive `listing_status` values. Here is a
synthetic call log for the 16 sampled listings, grouped by stratum
(`stratified_listing_sample()` appends strata in allocation order, so
the first 5 rows are `nppes+board`, the next 5 are
`nppes+board+society`, and the last 6 are `nppes+society`):

```{r calls}
sampled$disposition <- c(
  "Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "No-changed practices", "No-retired or no longer practicing medicine",
  "Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "No-changed practices", "No-not specified why",
  "Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "No-changed practices", NA, NA
)
sampled$reached <- c(
  rep(TRUE, 5),
  rep(TRUE, 5),
  TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, NA
)

calls <- classify_listing_status(sampled, map = ent_disposition_map())
calls[, c("stratum", "disposition", "reached", "listing_status", "invalid_reason")]
table(calls$listing_status)
```

A few more columns, added now so every one of them is already on
`calls` by the time `listing_validity_design()` captures it below: a
location-valid outcome derived independently of `listing_status` (for
the `outcome` example), a `rural` covariate (for the model example),
and the nested logical stages a validation cascade needs:

```{r extra-columns}
calls$location_valid <- dplyr::case_when(
  calls$listing_status == "confirmed_valid"   ~ TRUE,
  calls$listing_status == "confirmed_invalid" ~ FALSE,
  TRUE                                         ~ NA
)
calls$rural <- rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), 8)
calls$attempted_stage    <- !is.na(calls$reached)
calls$reached_stage      <- calls$reached %in% TRUE
calls$location_confirmed <- calls$physician_at_location == "confirmed_yes"
```

Two rows at the end are worth naming explicitly: `reached = FALSE`
with no disposition is an attempted-but-not-answered call -- a real
attempt, not a missing one -- and `reached = NA` with no disposition
is a listing that was never attempted at all. `classify_listing_status()`
tells these apart; a disposition string outside `ent_disposition_map()`
would stop the call entirely rather than silently falling into one of
the four statuses (`unmapped = "unresolved"` opts into the softer
behavior instead).

## Design-weighted estimates

`listing_validity_design()` wraps `survey::svydesign()` with the
`stratum`/`weight` columns already on `calls`:

```{r design}
design <- listing_validity_design(calls)
validity_estimates(design)
validity_estimates(design, by = "stratum")
```

A different outcome than the disposition-derived status -- for
example a location-valid flag from a separate survey item -- can be
estimated the same way via `outcome`, bypassing `status`/`level`
entirely:

```{r outcome}
validity_estimates(design, outcome = "location_valid")
```

## How much the unresolved listings could move the estimate

Two listings above are `unresolved` -- not reached, or reached with no
clean disposition. `validity_sensitivity_bounds()` reports what the
estimate would be if every one of them were valid, and separately if
every one of them were invalid, alongside the observed,
complete-case-only number -- and asserts the three are correctly
ordered before returning anything:

```{r bounds}
validity_sensitivity_bounds(calls)
```

## A survey-weighted model

`validity_model()` fits the definitive listings only (unresolved and
not-attempted are excluded, the same complete-case estimand as
`validity_estimates()`'s default) and returns odds ratios, not log-odds:

```{r model}
validity_model(design, ~ stratum + rural)
```

## Study-flow and cascade counts that are guaranteed to add up

`listing_flow_counts()` recomputes sampled/attempted/reached/definitive
counts from `calls` directly -- it does not trust `validity_estimates()`'s
numbers, so the two independently reconcile:

```{r flow}
listing_flow_counts(calls, by = "stratum")
```

`validation_cascade()` reports the same kind of staged counts, but for
any ordered sequence of nested logical columns, each expressed two
ways: as a share of the first stage, and conditional on the stage
immediately before it. Stages must actually nest -- a listing
confirmed at its location but never recorded as reached would stop the
call, since that is a data error, not a valid cascade:

```{r cascade}
validation_cascade(calls, stages = c("attempted_stage", "reached_stage", "location_confirmed"),
                    by = "stratum", weights = "weight")
```

## What this does and doesn't let you say

The estimate above is a design-weighted share of listings this
particular sample could confirm valid, with honest bounds on what the
unresolved listings could have done to it -- not a claim about every
physician in every registry, and not a claim that `board` or `society`
membership itself means anything about accuracy (see
`vignette("registry-overlap")`'s design-rules discussion for why that
is a deliberately separate question). A different study -- the
OB/GYN subspecialty study, say -- runs through exactly the same six
functions with a different disposition codebook
(`obgyn_disposition_map()`) and different registries; nothing above is
specific to ENT.
